originalTitle: Alan Jones trial live updates: crown prosecutor outlines case against former broadcaster as indecent assault trial begins
summary: Former 2UE and 2GB radio broadcaster is facing 22 charges. Jones, 85, has pleaded not guilty
content: Prosecutor details relationship between Jones and teenage athlete Wright is now detailing the relationship between Alan Jones and complainant M who met Jones when he was a 15-year-old accomplished athlete. The court has heard he invited complainant M to dinner and when he complimented him on the tableware Jones sent him a gift of the same tableware. On another visit when complainant M complimented the flowers, Jones sent him fresh flowers each week. The court heard Jones referred to the young man as “handsome man”, “superstar” and “champion”. Court hears allegations made by complainant C The court has also heard allegations made by complainant C, who worked at Alan Jones’ radio station 2GB, and as Jones’s personal driver. The prosecution alleged Jones would talk about C’s penis, “calling him ‘Donkey’ and saying things like ‘It’s not really that big is it?’ and ‘when can I see it?’” The court heard Jones, on several occasions, touched C on the penis, outside his clothes, and rubbed his hand up and down C’s penis as C drove him home from his radio program. C also alleges Jones would regularly kiss him when they were alone together in lifts, at Jones’s home at 1 Macquarie Street, and at the 2GB offices. Often, C was holding Jones’s jacket and briefcase at the time. C did not consent to any of Jones’s behaviour, prosecutor Georgina Wright told the court. Wright said the court would be presented with text messages sent by Jones to C, commenting on the “size of his penis, dismay at never having seen C’s penis” and declarations of love. Wright alleged to the court C did not invite or want to receive the messages but felt he had to reply because he was “concerned about his position in the media industry if he overtly rejected” Jones. Court told of allegations by complainant J Prosecutor Georgina Wright has told the court that while complainant J was driving the defendant to his Fitzroy Falls property Alan Jones put his hand on his penis, causing him to jump. Jones is then alleged to have put his hands down complainant J’s underpants and squeezed his penis. The defendant made comments about his penis and complainant J had an erection. When they got out of the car Jones grabbed complainant J and attempted to give him a kiss, the court heard. Wright alleged Jones asked him if it was OK and complainant J said no, I have never done anything like this. The trial has begun. The crown prosecutor, Georgina Wright, is first to give an opening statement before judge Glenn Walsh. She is outlining the charges against Alan Jones, starting with complainant J, who met Jones when he was 14 and broke an athletics record. He was interviewed by Jones on 2GB and Jones bought him a mobile phone and gave him his phone number, the court heard. Wright alleged before the court that Jones had told complainant J he should concentrate on his training and he would financially support him. He started giving him $400 a week, paid into his bank account once a fortnight. Over time it rose to $500 and then $600 a week. In 2003 Jones repeatedly told complainant J, the court heard, that he loved him, and he would kiss him on the mouth. It is the crown case that at no time did complainant J consent to the kissing or touching. Before the trial began today, days of pre-trial hearings were held to organise the schedule, clarify issues and determine the admissibility of certain evidence. On Friday, Alan Jones’ legal team attempted to prevent the media from directly reporting the evidence of complainant J, who is scheduled to give evidence later today. They argued that because the evidence is being heard “in-camera” – which means in private and is typically done in such cases to protect the identity of the alleged victim – it did not “permit publication”. But the judge, Glenn Walsh, rejected this application, stating that in-camera evidence does not prohibit the direct publication of it. He also noted that complainant J was not “fussed” by media reporting his evidence. The decision means the media will remain in the courtroom while complainant J gives evidence and can directly report that. However he will remain anonymised as complainant J in line with the right of all alleged victims of sexual offences to maintain their privacy. Alan Jones has walked into court, with the aid of a cane. He said hello to a few people waiting in the line to get into the courtroom. The court is still closed but populated with lawyers involved with the case – from both prosecution and defence sides – and now, the defendant. When he exited his car outside court, the media scrum flocked towards him. In that moment, as my colleague Ima Caldwell observed, he remained silent as reporters peppered him with questions: “How does it feel to have your day in court,” one asked. “What do you have to say to your alleged victims?” asked another. My colleague Ben Doherty, who is waiting outside the courtroom, says lawyers have begun to arrive, some wheeling carriages of documents. A line has built up outside of journalists and members of the public waiting for the courtroom to open. But not everyone is going to fit. The trial has been scheduled for a very small courtroom, despite the intense public and media interest. Media gathers outside Downing Centre I am outside Sydney’s downing centre this morning where a wall of media has gathered before Alan Jones’ trial. Cameras on shoulders and microphones out, crews and reporters are competing for a position to catch a glimpse of Jones when he arrives. Meanwhile, more reporters are lining up inside to grab one of the limited seats inside the courtroom. Alan Jones enjoyed his position at the top of media, political and sporting circles for the better part of four decades. The former English master rose to be a successful Wallabies coach, a prime ministerial speech writer and a top-rating shock jock who was both courted and feared by the political establishment. chineseTitle: 艾伦·琼斯审判实时更新：随着非礼审判的开始，皇家检察官概述了针对前广播公司的案件
chineseSummary: 前 2UE 和 2GB 无线电广播公司面临 22 项指控。 85 岁的琼斯不认罪
chineseContent: 检察官详细介绍了琼斯和青少年运动员之间的关系 赖特现在详细介绍了艾伦·琼斯和申诉人 M 之间的关系，申诉人 M 是在琼斯 15 岁时认识的，他是一名出色的运动员。法庭获悉，他邀请申诉人 M 共进晚餐，当申诉人 M 称赞他的餐具时，琼斯送给他同样的餐具作为礼物。另一次，当申诉人 M 称赞这些花时，琼斯每周都会送他鲜花。法庭获悉，琼斯称这名年轻人为“帅哥”、“超级巨星”和“冠军”。法庭听取了申诉人 C 的指控 法庭还听取了申诉人 C 的指控，他曾在艾伦·琼斯的 2GB 广播电台工作，并担任琼斯的私人司机。检方称，琼斯会谈论 C 的阴茎，“称他为‘驴’，并说‘其实没有那么大吧？’和‘我什么时候可以看到它？’”法庭获悉，琼斯多次在 C 开车送他听完广播节目回家时，在衣服外面触摸 C 的阴茎，并用手在 C 的阴茎上上下摩擦。 C 还声称，当他们单独在一起在电梯里、在麦格理街 1 号琼斯的家中以及在 2GB 办公室时，琼斯经常亲吻他。通常，C 当时拿着琼斯的夹克和公文包。检察官乔治娜赖特告诉法庭，C 并不同意琼斯的任何行为。赖特表示，法庭将收到琼斯发给 C 的短信，其中评论了“他的阴茎的大小，对从未见过 C 的阴茎感到沮丧”和爱的宣言。赖特向法庭声称，C 并未邀请或希望接收这些信息，但他觉得自己必须回复，因为他“担心如果他公然拒绝琼斯，他在媒体行业的地位会受到影响”。法庭听取了申诉人 J P 的指控
